title: Where the eyeballs are

unit.size: billion hours of human attention per day, worldwide

source.name: Digital attention deep-research report
source.note: Industry reports and research, 2021 to 2026. Every figure below is either stated in that report or arithmetic on figures stated in it, and each tile says which.

method.formula: size = reach x time. A tile's area is its audience multiplied by the time that audience gives it each day, expressed in billions of hours per day.

bases.stated: Both inputs are printed in the source. No arithmetic beyond a unit conversion.
bases.derived: Both inputs come from the source but one had to be converted or allocated. The chain is on the tile.
bases.estimated: An input is not in the source and an assumption was made. These tiles are hatched. Treat them as a shape, not a number.

method.exclusions: Watching other people play games (~8.5 h/week per player in the source) is not given its own tile, because those hours are already inside YouTube and Twitch. Counting them twice would inflate the chart by roughly 3.6 billion hours a day.

groups.label: Social and short-form
groups.note: 5.79B users, 69.9% of the world, averaging 2h21m a day. Children are that daily budget split by each platform's stated per-user time.

children.label: TikTok
children.chain: 53.8 min/day stated (34 h/month). 5.79B social users x 53.8 min / 60 = 5.19B h/day.

children.label: Facebook
children.chain: 19h47m/month stated = 1,187 min / 30.44 days = 39.0 min/day. x 5.79B / 60 = 3.76B h/day.

children.label: Instagram
children.chain: 15h50m/month stated = 950 min / 30.44 days = 31.2 min/day. x 5.79B / 60 = 3.01B h/day.

children.label: Everything else social
children.chain: The 141 min/day social budget less the 124.0 min the three named platforms account for = 17.0 min/day. x 5.79B / 60 = 1.64B h/day. X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Snapchat and every other platform the source does not break out are inside this tile rather than missing from the chart.

groups.label: Video
groups.note: Long-form and live. Sized on stated audience and stated time, so no allocation was needed.

children.label: YouTube
children.chain: 2.74B monthly users x 48.7 min/day / 60 = 2.22B h/day. Both figures stated.

children.label: Twitch
children.chain: 20.8B hours watched in 2024 / 365 = 57.0M h/day = 0.057B h/day. 224M monthly users stated.

groups.label: Messaging
groups.note: The largest single audience on the internet, and the least monetised minute on it.

children.label: WhatsApp
children.chain: 3.3B monthly users x 33 min/day / 60 = 1.82B h/day. Both figures stated.

groups.label: Gaming
groups.note: Time at the controls only. Time spent watching other people play sits under Video, where it is already counted.

children.label: Playing
children.chain: 3B players x 7.4 h/week / 7 = 3.17B h/day, which is 63.4 min/day each.

unsized.label: Search
unsized.why: The source gives reach and intent, not minutes. A query is seconds long and worth more than an hour of feed.

unsized.label: Email
unsized.why: 80 emails a day per user, no time budget published.

unsized.label: Podcasts and audio
unsized.why: Episode length is given as 30 to 60 minutes but frequency is not, and most of it is second-screen time anyway.

unsized.label: Subscription video
unsized.why: Subscriptions are households, not people, and no per-user daily figure is stated.

unsized.label: VR
unsized.why: Usage described as niche and growing, with no hours attached.

unsized.label: Voice assistants
unsized.why: Device count is not attention. Nobody publishes seconds spent talking to a speaker.

unsized.label: Wearables
unsized.why: Glance-level attention that no current measurement framework captures.

facts: Search ads run a 6.6% click-through rate. Social feed ads run 0.5 to 0.9%. The gap is intent, and it is roughly ten to one.
About 25% of podcast listeners say they bought something they heard advertised, which is the highest purchase response of any format in the source.
After Apple's App Tracking Transparency, click-through on heavily targeted Meta ads fell 37%.
55% of 18 to 39 year olds say they have replaced streaming time with social media.
